currentContext.business: Ion Exchange (India) Limited delivers integrated solutions across the water, wastewater and solid-waste value chain, combining engineering solutions, treatment technologies, resins, membranes, specialty chemicals, automation and lifecycle services through a single partner. The Engineering segment serves industrial operators and communities with seawater desalination, water recycling, Zero Liquid Discharge, ultra-pure and high-purity water and waste-to-energy systems plus operation and maintenance services; the Chemical segment supplies ion exchange resins, adsorbents, specialty process chemicals and customised treatment programmes; and the Consumer Products segment brings purified drinking water and decentralised waste management to households, real estate developments and institutions such as hotels, hospitals, educational institutions, laboratories, railways and defence establishments. The company sells across 28 states and 7 union territories in India and in 67 countries, with exports at 21% of turnover per its BRSR disclosure.

Engineering: Water recycling and process stream purification and concentration
Chemicals: Specialty process chemicals and customised treatment programmes
Consumer Products: Indion Quencher and Auto Quencher systems
MBR-based sewage treatment plants and New Generation STPs
Digital: Asset Health & Performance Monitoring (APM) platform using AI and Digital Twin

currentContext.expansion: The year's headline capacity event was the greenfield ion exchange resin manufacturing facility at Roha, where both cation and anion resin production were commissioned. The facility uses advanced non-solvent manufacturing technologies that support the company's Green Chemistry initiative and enable solvent-free ion exchange resins, and it was designed for resource efficiency with what the company describes as one of the lowest per-capita water consumption levels among ion exchange resin manufacturers plus extensive water recycling built on its own environmental engineering expertise; market acceptance of the products has been encouraging. In the Chemical segment the company also implemented process improvements to enhance pharmaceutical resin manufacturing capability, including capacity enhancement initiatives approved by regulatory authorities, while its manufacturing facilities continue to progress towards zero liquid discharge. In membranes, Phase II expansion of the Goa membrane manufacturing facility is currently under implementation and is expected to significantly enhance production capacity to address growing domestic and international demand; the Division also completed a technology transfer agreement with Mann+Hummel that strengthens PVDF UF and MBR membrane manufacturing, and installed and commissioned a 350 kWp rooftop solar project expected to avoid roughly 265 tonnes of CO2 a year. On the Engineering side, no new plant was announced: operational efficiency was attributed to earlier capacity expansions at Goa and Hosur and the integration of the Wada facility, alongside the SAP enterprise platform rollout across the Engineering business. The international expansion plan rests on expanded resin capacity at Roha, the membrane product line and manufacturing expansion at Goa, and manufacturing and blending units in Saudi Arabia and the UAE - including commissioning of blending units at Dammam to serve the GCC - with the UAE base carrying In Country Value (ICV) certification. Geographic build-out continues through team development in Thailand, Indonesia, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh and expansion into the Philippines and Vietnam. Project execution milestones during the year included the North Africa desalination projects entering final handover stages (scope included design, commissioning and supply of a 240 MLD SWRO skid), progress on EPC work for Tecnicas Reunidas, Saipem, NPCC and Tecnimont, Indian Oil Corporation projects moving towards commissioning, Har Ghar Jal Mission work, and closure of the Sri Lanka infrastructure project. No rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in this bundle in a usable form.

risks.risk: West Asia conflict and shipping-route disruption
risks.note: The outbreak of war in the Middle East on 28 February 2026 and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz darkened the global outlook and hit the company directly: planned dispatches of high-value Engineering contracts to GCC geographies were held up (customer clearances to proceed only came in Q1 FY2026-27 after cost adjustment and logistics-route realignment), and Chemical segment export shipments in March 2026 were disrupted, affecting fourth-quarter performance and margins.

risks.risk: Trade policy and tariff exposure on exports
risks.note: US reciprocal tariffs of 25% on Indian products and services announced in April 2025, followed by an additional 25% penal tariff on most of India's merchandise exports to the United States, sit against a global backdrop of greater protectionism and fragmentation that prompted a downward revision of India's growth forecast; the company states it has strategised to expand presence in overseas geographies with focused attention on its product business.

risks.risk: Input cost inflation and margin compression
risks.note: Chemical segment margins faced quarter-specific pressure from product mix, input cost pressures, rising and volatile logistics cost and Roha facility costs even as turnover improved sequentially and year-on-year; the stated mitigation is passing cost increases through to customers to rationalise the margin impact, which depends on competitive tolerance in an intensely competitive market.

risks.risk: Order inflow timing and large-EPC selection risk
risks.note: Order inflow and backlog were impacted by delayed finalisation of some large-value opportunities. Management explicitly stays cautious on selecting large EPC jobs, taking decisions objectively against a built-in dynamic risk identification and mitigation framework - an acknowledgement that project-business risk is concentrated in bid selection.

risks.risk: Counterparty credit and liquidity risk in the project business
risks.note: Risk-mitigating measures named are a robust screening mechanism to do business only with credit-worthy customers, prime focus on liquidity and positive operational cash flow, and control over discretionary spend - indicating receivables and working-capital exposure inherent to contract execution.

risks.risk: Dependence on government-funded municipal water programmes
risks.note: Performance under Jal Jivan Nigam remained muted on account of non-release of funds from the Water Boards, showing that a material demand pool is exposed to public-sector budget release cycles rather than to underlying demand.

The risk management framework explicitly covers continuous monitoring of cyber security risks, with a mitigation plan encompassing a business continuity plan should the risk materialise - reflecting rising dependence on SAP, cloud, AI and IoT platforms across the business.

risks.risk: Physical climate risk to supply chain and assets
risks.note: The BRSR materiality assessment records Climate Change and Energy Management as a risk with negative financial implications: extreme weather, floods and heat stress threaten supply chain continuity and asset integrity. Mitigation is continuous energy-efficiency improvement, transition from fossil fuels and increased adoption of renewable energy.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety in manufacturing and project sites
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR materiality table as a risk with negative financial implications: manufacturing and project execution environments carry inherent risks of occupational injuries, chemical exposure and work-related illness, with non-compliance risking incidents, regulatory action and reputational harm; mitigated through an OHS management system, hazard identification and safety audits, mandatory training, LTIFR/TRIR tracking and emergency drills.

risks.risk: Responsible sourcing and supply chain conduct
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR materiality table as a risk with negative financial implications: procurement spans a wide supplier base, and lapses in supplier environmental, labour or ethical standards expose the company to reputational, operational and regulatory risk, with evolving SEBI BRSR value-chain disclosure requirements increasing transparency obligations.

one-line thesis: Engineering margins remain pressured by delayed UP Jal Jeevan Mission execution and international project deferrals, while Roha chemical plant ramp-up is causing EBITDA compression; however, strong order inflows, budget tailwinds in solar/semiconductor/data centers, and long-term margin recovery from Roha create a turning point for FY27.

risks & watch-items: UP Jal Jeevan Mission fund delays; Roha ramp-up delays in certifications; semiconductor project profitability thresholds; rupee volatility; legacy project execution drag into FY27
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges near-term pain but emphasizes structural improvements, selective bidding, and long-term tailwinds from budget and global trends; confident in Roha’s sustainability edge
non-obvious takeaways: Roha is a zero-liquid discharge plant with circular design — 1/3 CAPEX dedicated to sustainability, making it a global benchmark; this justifies longer payback (4-5 yrs) and is a strategic moat

themes.title: Water & environmental-infra EPC
themes.need: AMRUT, Namami Gange and Jal Jeevan still define the pipeline, but Q1FY27 put a number on the funding freeze. WPIL's consolidated revenue rose 32% to INR 501cr while STANDALONE collapsed 37% to INR 115cr as domestic Jal Jeevan invoicing froze, with INR 300-350cr of JJM receivables pending (mostly West Bengal, some MP) and nil received in the quarter - management expects substantial inflow only in Q2/H2. The offsetting discovery is that the theme has quietly become international: WPIL's overseas revenue roughly doubled to INR 386cr, about 77% of consolidated, on PCI Africa's first full execution quarter plus Gruppo Aturia MENA demand, lifting consolidated EBITDA margin to 15.04%. EIEL carries an all-time-high order book (~6x revenue); WABAG on desalination/technology; JISLJALEQS/JISLDVREQS and MAHEPC add micro-irrigation and water-efficiency equipment; EMSLIMITED/SPMLINFRA/JASH/DENTA/ELECTCAST/AWHCL add sewerage, control equipment and ductile-iron piping. Execution conversion, not order intake, remains the binding constraint.
themes.driver: JJM/AMRUT fund releases unlocking billing (WPIL's INR 300-350cr receivable is the tracer); FY27 order inflow; desalination + NTPC BESS EPC ramp; international Africa/MENA execution.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Ion Exchange (India) Limited is an end-to-end water and environmental solutions company spanning engineering projects, ion exchange resins and specialty chemicals, and consumer water products, exporting to over 60 countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Ion Exchange (India) Limited delivers integrated solutions across the water, wastewater and solid-waste value chain, combining engineering solutions, treatment technologies, resins, membranes, specialty chemicals, automation and lifecycle services through a single partner. The Engineering segment serves industrial operators and communities with seawater desalination, water recycling, Zero Liquid Discharge, ultra-pure and high-purity water and waste-to-energy systems plus operation and maintenance services; the Chemical segment supplies ion exchange resins, adsorbents, specialty process chemicals and customised treatment programmes; and the Consumer Products segment brings purified drinking water and decentralised waste management to households, real estate developments and institutions such as hotels, hospitals, educational institutions, laboratories, railways and defence establishments. The company sells across 28 states and 7 union territories in India and in 67 countries, with exports at 21% of turnover per its BRSR disclosure.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Long-term industry drivers described as never stronger: water security, sustainability, digitalization, resource efficiency and industrial transformation
- New-age industries - semiconductors, electronics, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, data centres, battery manufacturing and green hydrogen - creating unprecedented demand for high-purity and ultrapure water systems and advanced wastewater management
- Climate change and the rising frequency of droughts, floods and extreme weather accelerating the need for resilient and decentralized water infrastructure
- Indian government programmes - Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT, Namami Gange, Har Ghar Jal Mission - plus Make in India driving municipal and industrial demand and growing adoption of water reuse and ZLD
- Engineering: healthy order bank and a robust solar order pipeline, with increased focus on semiconductors and data centres expected to support the long-term growth trajectory
- Membrane: market-share gains across refinery, fertiliser and steel, with the Mann+Hummel technology transfer and Goa Phase II expansion supporting growth
- Chemicals: margins under pressure from elevated raw material costs and intense domestic and international competition, with only marginal sales volume growth and modest export volume growth
- Resins: pharma resin growth, encouraging market acceptance of solvent-free resins from Roha, and new product development
- Consumer Products: product innovation, omni-channel and e-commerce reach, IoT-enabled softeners and an expanded dealer network sustaining growth across Home Water Solutions, Institutional and Rural
- MENA and GCC desalination and wastewater opportunity, supported by water scarcity and an ICV-certified UAE manufacturing base allowing participation as a local player
- Global macro backdrop volatile: 2025 growth projections cut from 3.3% to 2.8% on US tariff increases and policy shifts, revised modestly upward to 3% by July 2025, then darkened by the outbreak of war in the Middle East on 28 February 2026 and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz
- Engineering business supported by a healthy order bank and sustained opportunities across key growth sectors, with several significant orders secured from the solar sector
- A robust solar order pipeline combined with focused business development across high-growth industries is expected to support long-term Engineering growth
- Membrane Division secured significant orders from leading customers across refinery, fertiliser and steel sectors
- Consumer Products Institutional business order bookings increased by over 65%
- Rural business supported by significant order inflows from government and institutional customers for rural and municipal water treatment projects, and several orders for specialised water treatment systems across multiple states
- Consumer Products business cites a strong order pipeline supporting continued growth momentum
- Saudi Arabia operations secured major orders from blue chip corporations such as Almarai and Ma'aden, expected to significantly improve revenue and cash flow
- A subsidiary (name elided in this bundle) reports potential projects under bidding and closure that are expected to significantly improve revenue this year

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Engineering: margin compression from low-margin UP projects and international mix shift; Chemicals: Roha depreciation (Rs.17M Q3), rupee-driven input cost inflation (pass-through underway); Consumer: negative margin due to strategic A&P spend

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritize debt reduction (Roha loan); reinvest Consumer segment profits into A&P; selective EPC project funding; no dividends mentioned

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The year's headline capacity event was the greenfield ion exchange resin manufacturing facility at Roha, where both cation and anion resin production were commissioned. The facility uses advanced non-solvent manufacturing technologies that support the company's Green Chemistry initiative and enable solvent-free ion exchange resins, and it was designed for resource efficiency with what the company describes as one of the lowest per-capita water consumption levels among ion exchange resin manufacturers plus extensive water recycling built on its own environmental engineering expertise; market acceptance of the products has been encouraging. In the Chemical segment the company also implemented process improvements to enhance pharmaceutical resin manufacturing capability, including capacity enhancement initiatives approved by regulatory authorities, while its manufacturing facilities continue to progress towards zero liquid discharge. In membranes, Phase II expansion of the Goa membrane manufacturing facility is currently under implementation and is expected to significantly enhance production capacity to address growing domestic and international demand; the Division also completed a technology transfer agreement with Mann+Hummel that strengthens PVDF UF and MBR membrane manufacturing, and installed and commissioned a 350 kWp rooftop solar project expected to avoid roughly 265 tonnes of CO2 a year. On the Engineering side, no new plant was announced: operational efficiency was attributed to earlier capacity expansions at Goa and Hosur and the integration of the Wada facility, alongside the SAP enterprise platform rollout across the Engineering business. The international expansion plan rests on expanded resin capacity at Roha, the membrane product line and manufacturing expansion at Goa, and manufacturing and blending units in Saudi Arabia and the UAE - including commissioning of blending units at Dammam to serve the GCC - with the UAE base carrying In Country Value (ICV) certification. Geographic build-out continues through team development in Thailand, Indonesia, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh and expansion into the Philippines and Vietnam. Project execution milestones during the year included the North Africa desalination projects entering final handover stages (scope included design, commissioning and supply of a 240 MLD SWRO skid), progress on EPC work for Tecnicas Reunidas, Saipem, NPCC and Tecnimont, Indian Oil Corporation projects moving towards commissioning, Har Ghar Jal Mission work, and closure of the Sri Lanka infrastructure project. No rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in this bundle in a usable form.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges near-term pain but emphasizes structural improvements, selective bidding, and long-term tailwinds from budget and global trends; confident in Roha’s sustainability edge

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- End-to-end coverage of the entire water cycle, combining engineering solutions, treatment technologies, resins, membranes, specialty chemicals, automation and lifecycle services through a single trusted partner
- One of the broadest portfolios of ion exchange resins, adsorbents, specialty process chemicals and customised treatment programmes available in the market
- Execution credentials with international EPC contractors such as Tecnicas Reunidas, Saipem, NPCC and Tecnimont, plus large-scale desalination credentials from North Africa projects including a 240 MLD SWRO skid
- Export base across over 60 countries with exports contributing about a quarter of turnover, and an APAC presence built over three decades
- In-house R&D and proprietary environmental engineering expertise, evidenced at Roha by low per-capita water consumption and extensive water recycling systems
- Recurring, service-led revenue from a 24x7 service platform covering O&M, performance optimisation, upgrades, consumables and spares
- ZeroB consumer brand supported by an innovation pipeline, omni-channel and e-commerce reach and IoT-enabled products
- ICV-certified UAE manufacturing base enabling participation in local MENA and GCC projects as a local player
- Technology transfer agreement with Mann+Hummel strengthening PVDF UF and MBR membrane manufacturing capability
- In-house digital water intelligence stack, including the AI and Digital Twin based APM platform, HubSpot lead-to-order framework and SAP implementation across the Engineering business

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: UP Jal Jeevan Mission fund delays; Roha ramp-up delays in certifications; semiconductor project profitability thresholds; rupee volatility; legacy project execution drag into FY27

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Roha is a zero-liquid discharge plant with circular design — 1/3 CAPEX dedicated to sustainability, making it a global benchmark; this justifies longer payback (4-5 yrs) and is a strategic moat

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen technology leadership across ion exchange, membrane separation, advanced oxidation processes, PFAS remediation, green chemistry and digitally enabled water management, backed by investment in R&D, application engineering and process innovation
- Expand presence in sunrise industrial sectors where water quality is a critical manufacturing input - semiconductors, electronics, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, data centres, battery manufacturing and green hydrogen
- Deepen differentiation as an end-to-end water partner by combining engineering solutions, treatment technologies, resins, …
